title: Light-induced nonconservative static forces in many-body systems
authors: Jinze Li, Xuemei Yang, Zhiyuan Sun
abstract: In a quantum many-body system, a periodic drive can often generate effective static forces on the slow collective degrees of freedom. We study the static forces generated by light on electronic order parameters in solid-state systems. We show that the forces can have nonconservative components that originate from dissipation, i.e., optical absorption. This effect is demonstrated in two nontrivial examples. In excitonic insulators, via interband excitations, the light field generates a nonconservative force on the phase of the excitonic order parameter. This force leads to an acceleration of the phase, which manifests as a shift of the photon emission peak from an exciton condensate. In materials with an incommensurate charge density wave, a propagating light field generates a nonconservative force on the phase of its order parameter. It drives the charge density wave into sliding motion, leading to a DC electric current via topological Thouless pumping.
summary: This paper investigates how light can exert nonconservative static forces on collective order parameters in quantum materials like excitonic insulators and CDW systems. By linking these forces to optical absorption, the authors predict measurable effects, such as shifts in photon emission peaks or the generation of a DC current. The methodology relies on advanced many-body theoretical techniques applied to driven quantum systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on light-induced nonconservative static forces (NCSFs) acting on slow collective degrees of freedom within quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The light field generates nonconservative forces rooted in dissipation (optical absorption), which drive measurable phenomena like phase acceleration in excitonic insulators or DC current generation in charge density waves.
method: The analysis employs advanced diagrammatic techniques (e.g., triangular diagrams) within a Keldysh formalism to derive effective equations of motion and force terms for the order parameter phase.
model_or_system: The work examines general quantum many-body systems, specifically modeling excitonic insulators (EI) and materials exhibiting incommensurate charge density waves (CDW) driven by periodic light fields.
key_observables: Phase winding velocity (measured via photon emission peak shift in EIs) and DC electric current ($I_{CDW}$) in CDW systems.
important_parameters: Optical gap ($	ilde{E}_G$), light frequency ($\omega$), and the coupling strength related to dissipation.
main_assumptions: The NCSF is explicitly linked to dissipation (optical absorption), and the analysis often involves approximations in the slow-energy limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the NCSF field, the simulated phase evolution in EIs showing peak shifts, and the theoretical diagrams contributing to the force and current in CDW systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general concepts of NCSFs to specific derivations for EIs (phase dynamics) and then details the rigorous calculation of the force and current in CDW systems using Keldysh formalism and diagrammatic expansion.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical framework for understanding how light-matter interaction, specifically through dissipative processes, can induce directed, non-equilibrium motion in condensed matter order parameters, bridging quantum optics and solid-state physics.
